description: Same counterfactual reassignment as patch_reassignment_v1, run on PatchNAS's own raw (un-routed) patch output instead of DynaPatch-NoGate's. Decided 2026-09-04 (note/RESEARCH_STATE.md), executed 2026-09-05.
rq: RQ1 (extended): does destroying the failure-type-to-correction match hurt every per-input patch method, not just DynaPatch, i.e. is 'different failures need different repair directions' a general principle rather than a DynaPatch-specific one?
hypothesis: PatchNAS's patch head also produces a correction whose held-out repair rate depends on matching each failure to its own logit-space effect, not just on the effect's magnitude.
falsifier: The median RR_held advantage of the original assignment over global reassignment is at most 0.02, or fewer than 24 of 36 cells exceed the null 97.5th percentile.
support_rule: Support if the median advantage is greater than 0.05 and at least 30 of 36 cells exceed the null 97.5th percentile.

data.population: Rows where the frozen base prediction is wrong. patched_logits/patch_pred_raw are PatchNAS's own raw patch-head output, UNCONDITIONAL on its own router (routing is a separate, later decision -- not part of what this experiment tests).

compute.device: CPU analysis from saved logits, no model loading or GPU computation

stopping_rule: PROMOTE if the support rule passes; report alongside DynaPatch-NoGate's own result (patch_reassignment_v1) as the same test applied to a second method, not a win/loss comparison between the two.
